content:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Martinez (Searchlytics - Head of Search), Maya Chen (Searchlytics - Eng Manager), Derek O'Neal (Searchlytics - Data Scientist)

Summary:
Quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking endpoints for improving search relevance in Searchlytics product. Walkthrough of Console views, Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization), and example rerank flow. Customer asked about latency, cost tradeoffs, SSO, data residency and security (SOC2/KMS). Agreed next steps around POC dataset and pricing docs.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain points (Elastic + Pinecone hybrid, slow recall + noisy ranking)
- Hosted API embeddings + rerank demo
- Console: per-route metrics and trace for rerank
- Optimize suggestions: batching, caching, quantization recommendations
- Security: SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS, data retention
- POC scoping and success criteria

Action items (see metadata)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, you should be able to hear me, um, quick intro — I'm Jordan AE at Redwood, and with me is Priya our SE.
[00:00:12] Alex Martinez: Yep hear you, thanks Jordan. I'm Alex, head of search at Searchlytics, Maya and Derek are on.
[00:00:20] Maya Chen: hi all, thanks for the invite.
[00:00:25] Priya Nair: great, we'll run a 30-ish minute demo and leave time for Q&A, sounds good?
[00:00:31] Derek O'Neal: good for us.
[00:00:36] Jordan Lee: cool. Quick calibration — Alex, can you give a 2 min on current stack and main pain?
[00:00:42] Alex Martinez: sure, so we use Elastic as the primary inverted index for recall, then Pinecone for vector similarity for some features, um, but our rerank layer is 2-stage — it's kinda homegrown, runs on a small microservice, and it's not great for variety of queries, especially short queries where embeddings don't pick up nuance. Latency spikes in peak, cost is creeping up 'cause Pinecone scales on vector-heavy traffic.
[00:01:12] Jordan Lee: got it, makes sense. Are you open to hosted endpoints for both embeddings and reranking or would you prefer dedicated/private?
[00:01:19] Alex Martinez: initial goal is speed to iterate — hosted sounds fine, but we have to satisfy SSO and SOC2 considerations, and some customers ask for data residency.
[00:01:30] Priya Nair: totally, the hosted API supports enterprise SSO (SAML) and we have SOC 2 compliant processes, plus we can discuss Private if you need VPC or on-prem for data residency. For the demo I'll show hosted flow and Console so you can see the dashboards and the rerank path.
[00:01:48] Jordan Lee: ok jumping into the Console — sharing my screen (note: link to Console demo deck: https://redwood.app/demo/searchlytics)
[00:01:55] [screen share started]
[00:02:10] Priya Nair: in Console, you can see a per-route latency breakdown, token-level cost, and traces. This route here is a rerank endpoint that takes candidate docs + query embedding and runs a lightweight model to reorder.
[00:02:26] Maya Chen: quick q — do you support streaming tokens for rerank or is it batch?
[00:02:31] Priya Nair: rerank is typically synchronous per request — its latency is usually sub-200ms with our optimized models for short context, but you can batch upstream recall and use a separate bulk rerank job if throughput matters.
[00:02:44] Jordan Lee: note though that we use prefix/KV cache and continuous batching under the hood to keep per-token cost low when you have repeated prefixes or similar queries.
[00:02:55] Derek O'Neal: how do you handle model variants? Like lighter quantized vs full-precision?
[00:03:01] Priya Nair: good Q — we have a model catalog and runtime picks kernels based on architecture and sequence length; you can pin a variant or allow smart routing to pick quantized versions for cost-sensitive traffic and full precision for high-priority routes. Optimize will recommend quantization profiles per workload.
[00:03:18] Alex Martinez: do you have benchmarks vs Pinecone for recall+rerank? We care about recall quality and end-to-end latency.
[00:03:26] Priya Nair: we have a benchmark spreadsheet — I'll share it after the call. For rerank, you often see improvement by combining semantic recall (embeddings) with a lightweight reranker that looks at context and structured signals; end-to-end latency depends on your recall fanout and model size but common configs are 120-250ms p50 for hosted rerank on small models.
[00:03:45] [00:04:00] Jordan Lee: demo time — calling embeddings endpoint with a sample product query, showing vector response, then hitting rerank endpoint with top 10 candidates.
[00:04:10] [sound of typing]
[00:04:20] Priya Nair: ok so first call: POST /v1/embeddings with body — here's sample — and you'll see a 1536-d vector back. Note: we support multiple dims depending on model.
[00:04:36] Maya Chen: hmm, are dims fixed per model or tunable?
[00:04:40] Priya Nair: fixed per model. We also surface model profiles in the Console so you can pick dimension, latency profile, and cost estimate.
[00:04:52] [00:05:00] Jordan Lee: next we call /v1/rerank with query + candidates. The response includes score + rationale tokens if you enable structured output or tool-calling.
[00:05:12] Derek O'Neal: rationale tokens? like explanation?
[00:05:15] Priya Nair: it's a short structured blob — not a full explainable AI claim — more to help you debug why an item ranked higher. It's useful in A/B and eval loops.
[00:05:26] Alex Martinez: that could be helpful for our product team. How does billing look — per-token + per-embedding + rerank call?
[00:05:33] Jordan Lee: hosted billing typically combines per-embedding vector unit + per-token generation for rerank. We can model expected unit economics based on your QPS and typical recall fanout; I can send sample pricing.
[00:05:45] Maya Chen: our concern is cost at scale. If we do 200 req/s with 10 candidates each, it adds up. Any caching to reduce cost?
[00:05:54] Priya Nair: yes — automatic prefix and KV caching reduces repeat work, and Optimize suggests batching and cache TTLs. Also, you can route low-priority traffic to quantized model variants.
[00:06:06] Jordan Lee: also, Dedicated pools are an option if you want predictable throughput and lower unit cost at high volume. But initial POC is usually hosted to iterate faster.
[00:06:16] Alex Martinez: makes sense. For POC we'd like to try hosted first. Two questions on security: SSO and KMS integration.
[00:06:24] Priya Nair: we support SAML SSO at enterprise plan level, RBAC in Console, and KMS/HSM integrations for key management. Audit logs are available and we can export to your SIEM.
[00:06:36] Derek O'Neal: do you store raw queries/documents? We have PII concerns.
[00:06:40] Jordan Lee: by default we retain logs for 30 days but can adjust retention or disable retention for specific routes; with Private deployment or Dedicated you get more control. We also offer encryption at rest and in transit.
[00:06:53] Maya Chen: ok good.
[00:06:57] [00:07:00] Priya Nair: jumping to a live rerank example — showing a search for "wireless earbuds noise cancellation" and the top-10 candidates from recall. You can see the reranker reorders based on price, recency signals, and semantic match.
[00:07:15] [screen shows rerank response]
[00:07:22] Priya Nair: note the per-route dashboard shows median latency 145ms, p95 320ms, token cost breakdown, and a helpful trace that pins time in embedding, network, and rerank model.
[00:07:36] Alex Martinez: what's the usual way teams evaluate relevance improvements? We run offline metrics like MRR and NDCG.
[00:07:42] Priya Nair: we recommend baseline eval on sample queries (you can upload sets in Console), run A/B experiments and use our quality monitoring to detect regressions. Optimize can suggest changes if quality dips after a model change.
[00:07:55] Derek O'Neal: curious about rerank training — do you provide training pipelines or do we bring our own?
[00:08:00] Jordan Lee: currently we provide inference + eval tooling; training pipelines are typically customer-managed but we offer guidance on prompt/reranker design and can help with small custom fine-tuning recommendations via partners.
[00:08:12] Maya Chen: if we want to do a hybrid where recall is Elastic first then embeddings, how much engineering work to plug into Redwood endpoints?
[00:08:19] Priya Nair: minimal — you call embeddings endpoint with the doc vectors extracted from Elastic or with our embeddings and then pass candidates to rerank endpoint; we have SDKs and sample code (Node/Python) and we can provide a starter repo.
[00:08:33] Alex Martinez: can you show the example SDK code?
[00:08:36] Jordan Lee: sure — here's the snippet in the demo deck, I'll paste after — also link to a small repo we use in POCs. (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/po-repo) — note: link is demo placeholder.
[00:08:52] [00:09:00] Priya Nair: more on Optimize — it surfaces suggestions like batch size, model variant, cache TTL, and estimated cost delta. For your workload with many short queries, it might recommend smaller models for rerank and prefix caching for queries repeated across users.
[00:09:12] Derek O'Neal: do you do any automatic fallback if a model times out?
[00:09:15] Priya Nair: yes we have graceful degradation policies — fallback to a cheaper model and optional static ranking rules. You can configure canary and automatic fallback in Console.
[00:09:27] Maya Chen: what's the SLA for hosted?
[00:09:30] Jordan Lee: hosted has best-effort SLAs; Dedicated contracts come with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. For POC you'll be on hosted free credits or trial plan.
[00:09:43] Alex Martinez: ok. For POC success criteria: 10% net improvement in NDCG on our eval set and p50 rerank latency under 200ms. Is that reasonable?
[00:09:52] Priya Nair: yes that's reasonable — we'll help define the eval set and run baseline comparisons.
[00:09:58] [00:10:00] Jordan Lee: quick note on costs again — I'll build a simple cost model for your 200 QPS scenario and show live comparisons for hosted vs dedicated, including batching benefits.
[00:10:13] Alex Martinez: thanks.
[00:10:16] Maya Chen: another thing — we use Elastic snapshots and have geographic data zones. How does data residency play with hosted?
[00:10:23] Priya Nair: hosted supports region selection; for strict residency we may recommend Private deployment or Dedicated in a region with contractual controls. We can also restrict retention.
[00:10:36] Derek O'Neal: any gotchas on shard sizes for recall when combining with vectors?
[00:10:40] Priya Nair: that's more on Elastic side; for vectors we typically store embeddings in a vector DB or call embedding endpoint at ingest. Our SDKs show sample ingestion flows.
[00:10:51] [00:11:00] Jordan Lee: ok returning to Console to show traces and an example trace with a 180ms rerank.
[00:11:06] [screen shows trace timeline]
[00:11:12] Priya Nair: you can also hook traces into your observability via tracing hooks and open tracing headers.
[00:11:20] Alex Martinez: nice. Does Console expose token-level cost per route historically?
[00:11:25] Priya Nain: (mispronounced) yep — token-level and embedding-unit breakdown over time. Helpful for budgeting.
[00:11:33] Maya Chen: spelling of that name is fine, no worries.
[00:11:36] Derek O'Neal: any rate limit options? We might want burst policies.
[00:11:40] Jordan Lee: yes, rate limits, quotas and burst policies are configurable per API key and per-route. Dedicated gives much higher caps.
[00:11:49] Alex Martinez: ok we'll likely start POC with 10 QPS and then scale.
[00:11:54] [00:12:00] Priya Nair: last part — let's walk through a small evaluation flow in Console: upload queries, label preferences, run baseline and then import rerank results to compute MRR/NDCG.
[00:12:12] [screen shows eval UI]
[00:12:18] Priya Nair: here's an example where we ran a 2k query eval and saw NDCG uptick 12% post-rerank on a small catalog.
[00:12:26] Maya Chen: nice. Can we use our own metrics?
[00:12:29] Priya Nair: yes you can bring custom metrics, we can ingest results in CSV format.
[00:12:34] Derek O'Neal: about doc size — our product descriptions vary a lot, will that affect embeddings?
[00:12:40] Priya Nair: embeddings handle variable lengths; for very long docs we recommend chunking and storing chunk vectors and using rerank to reassemble. Optimize can recommend chunk sizes.
[00:12:52] [00:13:00] Jordan Lee: ok wrapping up with POC scope — propose: 4-week POC, up to 50k queries, baseline eval + rerank, hosted with free credits, success = 10% NDCG and p50 under 200ms. Thoughts?
[00:13:14] Alex Martinez: sounds good, want to confirm internal stakeholders but directionally yes.
[00:13:19] Maya Chen: timeline looks doable.
[00:13:22] Derek O'Neal: fine.
[00:13:25] [silence a few seconds]
[00:13:30] Priya Nair: ok final Q&A?
[00:13:33] Alex Martinez: one last — any examples of customers who did Elastic + hosted rerank and achieved improvements?
[00:13:39] Jordan Lee: yep we have a few case studies— I can share anonymized metrics where customers saw 8-20% NDCG improvements.
[00:13:48] Maya Chen: please share.
[00:13:51] Jordan Lee: will do.
[00:13:54] [00:14:00] Priya Nair: closing notes — I'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and sample rerank prompt set. Also include links to the SDK and Console quickstart.
[00:14:09] Jordan Lee: Jordan: I'll send pricing, SSO guide, and a proposed POC contract draft.
[00:14:16] Alex Martinez: great, we'll aim to have dataset and stakeholders by Friday.
[00:14:22] Maya Chen: yep.
[00:14:25] Derek O'Neal: thanks everyone.
[00:14:28] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up with invites for the POC kickoff.
[00:14:33] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attributions and minor OCR-like errors (e.g., Priya Nain vs Priya Nair) — left in to reflect real Fireflies artifacts.
